issues.title: Features package imports from trpc
issues.description: The rule requires that the features package does not import from trpc, but permission-check.service.ts imports TRPCError from @trpc/server
issues.rule_name: Prevent Circular Dependencies Between Core Packages

issues.title: orgId parameter not propagated in getTeamIdsWithPermission
issues.description: The method getTeamIdsWithPermission accepts an orgId parameter to scope permission checks to a specific organization, but it fails to pass this parameter to the underlying getTeamIdsWithPermissions method. This causes organization scoping to be ignored when checking single permissions, allowing users to potentially access teams from all organizations instead of only the specified one. The bug breaks the core security feature introduced in this PR where organization-scoped permission checks were meant to restrict access based on orgId.

issues.title: Incomplete orgId filtering in PBAC child team query
issues.description: In the SQL query for getTeamsWithPBACPermissions, the WHERE clause for child teams is missing a check for child."parentId" = ${orgId}. The original PR added this condition to properly scope child teams when an orgId is provided, but this implementation only checks org."id" and child."id", missing the case where a child team's parent should match the orgId. This causes the query to incorrectly exclude child teams whose parentId matches the specified orgId, breaking the inheritance model where organization permissions should propagate to child teams.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
SELECT DISTINCT child."id"
FROM "Membership" m
INNER JOIN "Role" r ON m."customRoleId" = r.id
INNER JOIN "Team" org ON m."teamId" = org.id
INNER JOIN "Team" child ON child."parentId" = org.id
WHERE m."userId" = ${userId}
  AND m."accepted" = true
  AND m."customRoleId" IS NOT NULL
  AND (${orgId}::bigint IS NULL OR org."id" = ${orgId} OR child."id" = ${orgId})

issues.title: Authorization bypass when filtering multiple userIds including current user
issues.description: The isCurrentUser check was changed from a strict equality check (filters.userIds.length === 1 && user.id === filters.userIds[0]) to a loose inclusion check (filters.userIds.includes(user.id)). This allows a user to bypass permission checks by including their own userId in a list alongside other userIds they don't have permission to access. For example, if a user requests bookings for [ownUserId, unauthorizedUserId], the check passes even though they lack permission for the unauthorized user, allowing them to access bookings they shouldn't see.

issues.title: Service file uses forbidden `.service.ts` suffix
issues.description: Rule 1 forbids dot-suffix filenames like `.service.ts`. This service lives in `permission-check.service.ts` instead of a PascalCase `<Entity>Service.ts` filename matching the class name (e.g., `PermissionCheckService.ts`).

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #25434 - fix: get bookings handler for pbac and fallback roles

structured_output.summary:
This PR changes the bookings `getBookings` handler so it no longer queries ADMIN/OWNER memberships directly. It now calls `PermissionCheckService.getTeamIdsWithPermission("booking.read")` with ADMIN/OWNER as fallback roles, then works out the accessible event types and team members from the team IDs that come back. It also adds an optional `orgId` parameter through the service, the interface and `PermissionRepository`, and splits the raw SQL into two private helpers that each take an org-scope predicate.

Moving to PBAC is the right direction and the refactor is clean. But two changes make authorization worse than before. First, the `userIds` guard was loosened from "exactly my own ID" to "contains my own ID". Any user can now read anyone's bookings by sending `userIds: [me, victim]`. Second, `PermissionRepository.getTeamIdsWithPermission` accepts `orgId` but never passes it to `getTeamIdsWithPermissions`, so the org scoping this PR exists to add never reaches the bookings handler. The new tests don't cover either case, mostly because they assert `resolves.not.toThrow()` and only use `orgId: null`.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The `isCurrentUser` change is an authorization bypass: any authenticated user can read bookings for arbitrary user IDs. Separately, `orgId` is silently dropped in the singular repository method. Both need to be fixed, with tests, before merge.

architecture.overview:
`getBookings` in `get.handler.ts` builds a UNION of Kysely queries over `Booking`/`Attendee`/`BookingSeat`. Before this PR, the extra scope (bookings of team/org members and of team event types) came from a Prisma query for memberships where the user is ADMIN/OWNER, filtered to `user.orgId`.

After this PR, the scope comes from `PermissionCheckService.getTeamIdsWithPermission({ permission: 'booking.read', fallbackRoles: [ADMIN, OWNER], orgId })`. The service calls `PermissionRepository`, which runs two raw SQL queries in parallel: one for PBAC custom-role teams and one for fallback-role teams where PBAC is off. Both now take an optional `orgId` predicate. The handler then turns the team IDs into event-type IDs (`getEventTypeIdsFromTeamIdsFilter`) and member IDs and emails (`getUserIdsAndEmailsFromTeamIds`), and uses them in the existing booking sub-queries 4–7.
steps: Start at `getHandler` → `getAllUserBookings` → `getBookings` in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/get.handler.ts`. The user context carries `id`, `email` and `orgId`.
`getBookings` now builds a `PermissionCheckService` and asks for the team IDs where the user has `booking.read`, with ADMIN/OWNER as fallback roles and `orgId` set from the user's profile.

`PermissionCheckService.getTeamIdsWithPermission` validates the permission string and calls `PermissionRepository.getTeamIdsWithPermission`. That method forwards to `getTeamIdsWithPermissions`, which runs `getTeamsWithPBACPermissions` and `getTeamsWithFallbackRoles` in parallel and unions the results.
The team IDs are turned into event-type IDs (direct plus managed children) and member IDs/emails through Prisma. This replaces the old membership-relation filters.

If the `userIds` filter is present, it is authorized against the accessible member IDs, with an exception for the current user. After that the UNION booking queries (1–7) are built and run through Kysely.

findings.title: `userIds` guard now lets anyone read arbitrary users' bookings by including their own ID
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/get.handler.ts` (lines ~144-159), `isCurrentUser` was changed to `filters.userIds.includes(user.id)`. Any request that includes the caller's own ID now skips the FORBIDDEN check, and bookings for every other listed user are returned. Fix the guard so each requested userId must be the current user or appear in `allAccessibleUserIds`. For example, fold `userId === user.id` into the `.every()` predicate and drop the separate `isCurrentUser` short-circuit, or restore the old `length === 1 && user.id === filters.userIds[0]` check. Add a test in `get.handler.test.ts` that calls `getBookings` with `userIds: [1, 4]` (user 1 is the caller and user 4 is not accessible) and expects a FORBIDDEN rejection.

findings.title: `getTeamIdsWithPermission` drops `orgId`, so org scoping never reaches the bookings handler
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/pbac/infrastructure/repositories/PermissionRepository.ts` line 222, `getTeamIdsWithPermission` destructures `orgId` but does not pass it to `getTeamIdsWithPermissions`, so org scoping is silently lost for every caller of the singular method, including the bookings `get.handler.ts`. Pass `orgId` through. Then add an integration test in `packages/features/pbac/infrastructure/repositories/__tests__/PermissionRepository.integration-test.ts` that mirrors the existing 'should filter teams by orgId when provided' test but calls `getTeamIdsWithPermission` (singular), so the scoping is covered on that path too.

findings.title: New handler tests mostly assert nothing meaningful
findings.body:
Several tests in the new suite can't fail for the behavior they describe:

::code{file="packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/get.handler.test.ts" lines="260-278"}

- `resolves.not.toThrow()` on a resolved promise only checks that the call didn't reject. It doesn't verify which bookings or queries were built. This applies at lines 277, 299 and 333.
- The two tests named "should combine PBAC permissions and ADMIN/OWNER roles" and "should use fallback ADMIN/OWNER roles…" mock the service's return value. They never exercise PBAC versus fallback logic, so their names claim coverage they don't have.
- "Event type filtering" and "User IDs and emails retrieval" only assert `toHaveBeenCalled()`, not that the right `teamId: { in: [...] }` was passed.
- Every case uses `orgId: null`, so nothing checks that `orgId` is forwarded. That is why the dropped-`orgId` bug passes. The mixed `userIds: [self, other]` case is also missing, which is why the guard regression passes.

At minimum, add assertions on the `where` arguments passed to `prisma.user.findMany` / `prisma.eventType.findMany`. Also add a test with `user.orgId` set that checks the service receives `orgId`, and a FORBIDDEN test for a mixed `userIds` list.
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/get.handler.test.ts`, strengthen the PBAC tests: (1) replace `resolves.not.toThrow()` (lines ~277, 299, 333) with assertions on observable outputs or on the `where` args passed to `prisma.user.findMany`/`prisma.eventType.findMany` (e.g. `teams.some.teamId.in` equals the mocked team IDs); (2) add a case with `user.orgId = 5` that asserts `getTeamIdsWithPermission` is called with `orgId: 5`; (3) add a case with `userIds: [1, 4]` where 1 is the caller and 4 is not accessible, and assert a FORBIDDEN rejection.

findings.title: Org-scope predicates in the child-team branches are redundant or odd
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/pbac/infrastructure/repositories/PermissionRepository.ts`, simplify the org-scope predicate in both child-team UNION branches (lines ~309 and ~357) to `(${orgId}::bigint IS NULL OR org."id" = ${orgId})`. The other OR terms are either implied by the `child.parentId = org.id` join or can never match for an organization. Also remove the duplicated `@param orgId` line in the `getTeamsWithFallbackRoles` JSDoc. Run the PermissionRepository integration tests to confirm they still pass.

findings.title: Unused `TRPCError` import added to PermissionCheckService
findings.body:
`TRPCError` is imported but never used in the service. The import also pulls a tRPC dependency into a `features/pbac` domain service, which should stay transport-agnostic.

::diff{file="packages/features/pbac/services/permission-check.service.ts" lines="1-7"}
findings.fixPrompt: Remove the unused `import { TRPCError } from "@trpc/server";` from `packages/features/pbac/services/permission-check.service.ts` (line 6). The service doesn't use it, and the features/pbac layer shouldn't depend on tRPC.

findings.title: Reusing `getEventTypeIdsFromTeamIdsFilter` removes duplicated logic
findings.body: Dropping `getEventTypeIdsWhereUserIsAdminOrOwner` in favour of the existing `getEventTypeIdsFromTeamIdsFilter` (which covers both direct team event types and managed child event types through `parent.teamId`) keeps the old coverage and removes about 40 duplicated lines. The early return for an empty list in `getUserIdsAndEmailsFromTeamIds` also saves a pointless query for users with no team permissions. Splitting the repository SQL into `getTeamsWithPBACPermissions` and `getTeamsWithFallbackRoles` makes the two permission paths much easier to read.
